summary: In this story, two brothers who constantly argue over chores must set aside their rivalry and cooperate to build a simple wooden footbridge so their younger siblings can safely reach school after a flood.
introduce: Act out a short mime, such as checking your watch and tapping your foot, and ask students how you feel and how they know. Explain that in “The Brothers Who Built a Bridge” they will use clues in the same way to work out what the writer does not say directly.

keyTerms.def: to work together with someone to get something done
a long, flat piece of wood used for building
a narrow way for walking from one place to another

challengeTerms.def: to work jointly with one or more people on a shared task or project
strongly and solidly built, not likely to break or fall apart
an agreement reached when each side gives up part of what it wanted

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that siblings who argue a lot can never learn to work well together? Use evidence from the story to explain.
Explain how Saad and Faisal's relationship changed from the beginning of the story to the end.
struggling: Pre-teach cooperate, plank, and path with pictures or gestures, then let weak readers answer “What clue tells you that?” questions using sentence starters.
gifted: Challenge advanced readers to use collaborate, sturdy, and compromise in a short paragraph that makes an inference that the story does not state and support it with two clues.
